claim: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of 50 papers in the field of cancer biology published between 2010 and 2012.
source: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of 50 papers in the field of cancer biology published between 2010 and 2012.
evidence: This is a statement about the project's goals and scope, presented as factual information about the project design.

claim: Sirota et al. published 'Discovery and Preclinical Validation of Drug Indications Using Compendia of Public Gene Expression Data' in Science Translational Medicine in 2011.
source: 'Discovery and Preclinical Validation of Drug Indications Using Compendia of Public Gene Expression Data' by Sirota et al., published in Science Translational Medicine in 2011 ( Sirota et al., 2011 ).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the original publication.

claim: Cimetidine is a histamine-2 (H2) receptor agonist commonly used to treat peptic ulcers.
source: cimetidine, a histamine-2 (H2) receptor agonist commonly used to treat peptic ulcers ( Kubecova et al., 2011 )
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kubecova et al., 2011.

claim: Sirota and colleagues predicted that cimetidine would be effective against lung adenocarcinoma.
source: Sirota and colleagues. tested a proof of concept experiment validating their prediction that cimetidine, a histamine-2 (H2) receptor agonist commonly used to treat peptic ulcers ( Kubecova et al., 2011 ), would be effective against lung adenocarcinoma (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is stated as a prediction made by the original authors, referencing their experimental validation.

claim: Sirota and colleagues predicted that cimetidine would not be efficacious against renal carcinoma.
source: As a control they also tested the effects of cimetidine against renal carcinoma, for which it was not predicted to be efficacious (Supplemental Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated as a prediction made by the original authors, used as a control experiment.

claim: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology is a collaboration between the Center for Open Science and Science Exchange.
source: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology is a collaboration between the Center for Open Science and Science Exchange
evidence: This is a factual statement about the organizational structure of the project.

claim: The results of the replications will be published by eLife.
source: the results of the replications will be published by eLife
evidence: This is a statement about the publication plan for the replication results.

claim: Sirota and colleagues hypothesized that extant drugs could be repurposed to target alternative diseases to improve efficiency in the search for new treatments.
source: Sirota and colleagues tested their hypothesis that extant drugs could be repurposed to target alternative diseases; if so, this could improve efficiency in the search for new treatments.
evidence: This describes the hypothesis tested in the original study.

claim: Sirota and colleagues compared data from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) to determine gene expression signatures of diseases.
source: They compared data from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO)—which they used to determine gene expression signatures of diseases—to data from the Connectivity Map
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the original study.

claim: The Connectivity Map tracks the changes in mRNA expression caused by 164 drugs.
source: data from the Connectivity Map, which tracks the changes in mRNA expression caused by 164 drugs
evidence: This describes the content and scope of the Connectivity Map database.

claim: Sirota and colleagues created a similarity score to describe how similar the changes in mRNA expression were between each drug and each disease.
source: By comparing these two mRNA expression sets, Sirota and colleagues created a similarity score to describe how similar the changes in mRNA expression were between each drug and each disease.
evidence: This describes the analytical approach used in the original study.

claim: Sirota and colleagues theorized that a similarity score close to −1 (exactly opposite signatures) might indicate that the drug could treat the disease.
source: They theorized that a similarity score close to −1 (exactly opposite signatures) might indicate that the drug could treat the disease.
evidence: This describes the theoretical framework used in the original study.

claim: Cimetidine is an H2 receptor blocker commonly used to treat gastric ulcers by reducing the production of stomach acid.
source: cimetidine, an H2 receptor blocker commonly used to treat gastric ulcers by reducing the production of stomach acid (Kubecova et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kubecova et al., 2011.

claim: Mice treated with cimetidine showed a dose-dependent reduction in tumor size after 12 days of treatment in A549 lung adenocarcinoma xenografts.
source: Mice treated with cimetidine showed a dose-dependent reduction in tumor size after 12 days of treatment.
evidence: This describes the results from the original study's Figure 4C and D.

claim: Cimetidine had no effect on the growth of ACHN renal carcinoma cells in xenograft models.
source: In Supplemental Figure 1, they also treated ACHN renal carcinoma cells with cimetidine, although cimetidine was not predicted to treat this cancer line. They observed no effect of cimetidine on the growth of this cancer cell line.
evidence: This describes the results from the original study's Supplemental Figure 1.

claim: The conclusions that can be drawn from the original experiments are limited by the fact that only a single cell line was tested with only a single drug.
source: However, the conclusions that can be drawn from these experiments are limited by the fact that only a single cell line was tested with only a single drug.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of the experimental design.

claim: No direct replication of the experiments presented in Sirota and colleagues' Figure 4C and D or Supplemental Figure 1 has been reported to date.
source: To date, no direct replication of the experiments presented in Sirota and colleagues' Figure 4C and D or Supplemental Figure 1 has been reported.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of replication studies in the literature.

claim: Stoyanov and colleagues reported that cimetidine reduced proliferation of A459 cells activated with histamine in vitro.
source: However, Stoyanov and colleagues did examine the effect of cimetidine on growth of A459 cells activated with histamine and reported that cimetidine did reduce proliferation in vitro (Stoyanov et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Stoyanov et al., 2012.

claim: An exploratory analysis of a cohort of diabetic patients demonstrated a decreased risk of developing lung cancer, specifically adenocarcinoma, in patients who took over-the-counter H2 receptor blockers, including cimetidine.
source: An exploratory analysis of a cohort of diabetic patients demonstrated a decreased risk of developing lung cancer, specifically adenocarcinoma, in patients who took over-the-counter H2 receptor blockers, including cimetidine (Hsu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hsu et al., 2013.

claim: The replication experiment will use at least 12 mice per group for a final power of 82.4%.
source: This experiment will use at least 12 mice per group for a final power of 82.4%.See 'Power calculations' for details.
evidence: This is based on statistical power calculations performed for the replication study design.

claim: A549 cells are maintained in F-12 Ham's medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 2 mM sodium pyruvate and 1 μM lipoic acid, based on ATCC recommendations.
source: A549 cells are maintained in F-12 Ham's medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 2 mM sodium pyruvate and 1 μM lipoic acid, based on ATCC recommendations.
evidence: This is based on standard cell culture protocols from ATCC.

claim: ACHN cells are maintained in EMEM supplemented with 10% FBS, 2 mM glutamine and 1 mM sodium pyruvate, based on ATCC recommendations.
source: ACHN cells are maintained in EMEM supplemented with 10% FBS, 2 mM glutamine and 1 mM sodium pyruvate, based on ATCC recommendations.
evidence: This is based on standard cell culture protocols from ATCC.

claim: All cells are grown at 37°C/5% CO2.
source: All cells are grown at 37°C/5% CO2.
evidence: This is a standard cell culture condition.

claim: 5 × 10^6 cells will be injected into the upper flank of 4–6-week-old female SCID mice.
source: Inject 5 × 106 cells (i.e., 100 µl of cell suspension) into the upper flank of 4–6-week-old* female SCID mice.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol for xenograft creation.

claim: Tumor volume is defined as mm³ = 0.52 × [width (cm)]² × height (cm).
source: Volume is defined as mm3 = 0.52 × [width (cm)]2 × height (cm).
evidence: This is a standard formula for calculating tumor volume.

claim: Treatment will be initiated when tumor reaches a minimum of 100 mm³ in volume (estimated time 2–3 weeks).
source: When tumor reaches a minimum of 100 mm3 in volume (estimated time 2–3 weeks#), initiate treatment.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol for treatment initiation.

claim: Treatment will continue for 11 days after tumors reach 100 mm³.
source: When tumor reaches a minimum of 100 mm3 in volume (estimated time 2–3 weeks#), initiate treatment. Continue treatment for 11 days past this point.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol duration.

claim: Mice will be euthanized if they appear in undue distress according to the replicating lab's guidelines or if the animal has lost >20% body weight.
source: Mice shall be euthanized if they appear in undue distress according to the replicating lab's guidelines; if the animal has lost >20% body weight.

claim: The replication attempt will not include the 25 mg/ml or 50 mg/ml cimetidine treatment groups from the original study.
source: The replication attempt will encompass the PBS control, the doxorubicin control and the highest dose of cimetidine (100 mg/kg). It will not include the 25 mg/ml or 50 mg/ml cimetidine treatment groups.
evidence: This describes a known difference between the original and replication protocols.

claim: The original study performed injections of 5 × 10^6 cells per microliter of PBS.
source: While the original study performed injections of 5 × 106 cells per microliter of PBS
evidence: This describes the original study's protocol.

claim: The replication will inject 5 × 10^6 cells suspended in 100 µl PBS on the advice of the replicating lab.
source: on the advice of the replicating lab we will inject the same number of cells but suspended in 100 µl PBS.
evidence: This describes a modification to the protocol based on expert advice.

claim: All data obtained from the experiment will be made publicly available, either in the published manuscript or as an open access dataset available on the Open Science Framework.
source: All data obtained from the experiment—raw data, data analysis, control data and quality control data—will be made publicly available, either in the published manuscript or as an open access dataset available on the Open Science Framework (https://osf.io/hxrmm/).
